original_question: Let K be compact and assume the weak and norm Borel sigma-algebras on C(K) coincide, so Bo(C(K), w) = Bo(C(K)). Does it follow that the pointwise and norm Borel sigma-algebras also coincide, meaning Bo(C(K), T_p) = Bo(C(K))?
target_in_paper: Problem 2.5 (Marciszewski-Pol) in Section 2.2: Let K be compact such that Bo(C(K), w) = Bo(C(K)). Does the equality Bo(C(K), T_p) = Bo(C(K)) hold?
correct_elements: Your draft identifies the correct object C(K), the correct hypothesis Bo(C(K), w) = Bo(C(K)), and the correct conclusion being asked about, namely whether Bo(C(K), T_p) = Bo(C(K)). This is essentially the exact open problem stated in the paper.
missing_details: The paper's standing convention is that all topological spaces are Hausdorff, so K should be stated as a compact Hausdorff space.
The paper works with real Banach spaces, so C(K) is the real Banach space of continuous real-valued functions on K.
Bo(C(K)) denotes the Borel σ-algebra for the norm topology on C(K), i.e. the topology of uniform convergence coming from the supremum norm.
T_p should be defined explicitly as the topology of pointwise convergence on K.
To be fully stand-alone, the question should quantify over every compact K satisfying the hypothesis and should not leave the topologies implicit.
refined_question: Let K be a compact Hausdorff space, and let C(K) be the real Banach space of continuous real-valued functions on K equipped with the supremum norm. Denote by w the weak topology on C(K), by T_p the topology of pointwise convergence on K, by Bo(C(K), w) and Bo(C(K), T_p) the corresponding Borel σ-algebras, and by Bo(C(K)) the Borel σ-algebra of the norm topology. If Bo(C(K), w) = Bo(C(K)), must it follow that Bo(C(K), T_p) = Bo(C(K))?
justification: The draft is aiming at the paper's Problem 2.5 in Section 2.2, page 6. The nearby context in equation (2.1) on page 6 sets up the three relevant Borel σ-algebras on C(K): those coming from the pointwise, weak, and norm topologies. Section 2.1, page 5 defines T_p as the topology of pointwise convergence on K, and the notation section on page 1 states that all topological spaces are Hausdorff and all Banach spaces are real. So the only refinements needed are to make those conventions explicit and to spell out that Bo(C(K)) is the norm-Borel σ-algebra. No broader reformulation is warranted, because the paper asks exactly this implication and nothing more.
